sentences.text:
Babbu Saroj And 7 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5
February, 2025

Author: Samit Gopal
Bench: Samit Gopal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:16381
Court No. - 78
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 16538 of 2024
Applicant :- Babbu Saroj And 7 Others
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Ali Hasan,Istiyaq Ali
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manava Nand Chaurasiya
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List revised.

2. Heard Sri Istiyaq Ali, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Manava Nand Chaurasiya, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, Sri V.D. Ojha, learned counsel for the State and perused the records.
3.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants-Babbu Saroj,
Brijlal Saroj, Sunita Devi, Sunita Saroj, Geeta Saroj, Muneem Saroj, Mahendra Saroj and Raju Saroj with the prayer to allow the present application and quash the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 457 of 2024 arising out of Case Crime No. 692 of 2022 under Sections 498A, 323, 506, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Nawabganj, District Allahabad pending before A.C.J.M-09,
Allahabad including charge-sheet dated 22.01.2023 and supplementary charge-sheet dated Babbu Saroj And 7 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190685839/
1 26.07.2023 and cognizance order dated 21.03.2024 and with the further prayer to stay the further proceedings of aforesaid case, during the pendency of present application.
4. The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court vide order dated 20.5.2024 for making an effort between the parties for settling their disputes amicably.
The dispute between the parties is matrimonial in nature.
5. As per the office report dated 4.2.2025, a report from the Mediation Centre of this Court is on record.

6. As per report of Mediation Centre dated 11.9.2024, the parties have entered into an interim settlements dated 23.8.2024 and 4.9.2024 and have amicably settled their dispute and decided to live separately and in this regard they have filed a petition u/s 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court concerned and the same is registered as Case No.1867 of 2024 and further agreed to withdraw the cases going on between them.
7.

From perusal of the report of Mediation Centre of this Court, it appears that in pursuance of the said order the mediation proceedings were taken up which ended in a settlement between the parties and the Mediation succeeded.
The parties have settled their grievances and even the dispute arising in the present matter.

The parties have agreed to withdraw the cases going on between them,
the said fact is mentioned in para 7 (g) of the said mediation report.
8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned counsel for the State
have no objection to the said proposition.

9. The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties,
is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.

10. From perusal of the records and the law laid down by the Apex Court on the subject matter, the present case is a good case for exercising powers by this Court to quash the proceedings as prayed for by the applicant(s).
11.
The present application is allowed.
12. The entire proceedings of the aforesaid case, charge sheet, supplementary charge sheet as well as cognizance order passed in the aforesaid case are hereby quashed.
